newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks gain ground, Tokyo in doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks gain ground, Tokyo in doldrums.

text.p: Bullish Hong Kong stocks took an early dive on Wednesday then recovered to finish sharply higher, while Tokyo struggled to keep even in an atmosphere of political uncertainty.
The picture across the rest of Asia was equally mixed with Singapore and Taiwan gaining and Seoul, Australia and New Zealand slipping.
Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 fought its way back up to the 21,000-point level after being battered throughout the day by bouts of selling, brokers said.
It closed 41.53 points or 0.20 percent at 21,082.15. Its December futures were down 70 points at 21,100.
"The Nikkei average is stuck in a box around the 21,000 level and will stay so until the political scenery clears," said Masayuki Matsumoto, a Daiichi Securities analyst.

Hopes that the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), the dominant partner in Japan's outgoing coalition, would win an overall majority in the Lower House of parliament prompted buying last week ahead of Sunday's general election.
When the LDP failed to secure the majority, the market's mood palled as the prospect of a shaky new coalition framework chilled investor sentiment, brokers said.
Discouraged investors and dealers especially moved to dissolve their longs.
Hong Kong stocks got off to a poor start, with the Hang Seng Index dipping by as much as 76 points in the morning session.
But buying momentum on rising turnover in the afternoon saw the index end at its high of the day of 12,492.37, up 47.71 points or 0.38 percent.
"The sell-off this morning was very unconvincing," said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia."Nobody wants to sell this market."
Other brokers were equally bullish.
"The market has a chance to test the 12,600 level this week. It's still in a healthy mode," said P.C. Wong, director of Hing Feng Futures.
Singapore's key Straits Times Index closed 7.61 points or 0.37 percent higher at 2,046.45 points and Taiwan gained 10.76 points or 0.17 percent to close at 6426.30.

Seoul lost 7.24 points or 0.77 percent to close at 3049.59 and the picture was equally glum in Australia and New Zealand. Australia's All Ordinaries slipped 6.9 points or 0.29 percent to 2346.7 and New Zealand lost 29.28 points or 1.25 percent to 2320.39.
Bombay continued its strong run and was up 103.44 points or 3.2 percent to 3,330.57 near the close. This followed a 96.92- point surge on Tuesday.
The Thai bourse took a break from its tortuous climb back over the past five days and was closed on Wednesday for a public holiday.
The dollar traded at 112.83/88 yen and 1.5243/48 marks at 1130 GMT, compared with New York's previous close of 112.30/40 yen and 1.5243/48 marks.
In Singapore, SIMEX Brent December futures were trading at $24.53 in late afternoon.
In Hong Kong bullion ended at US$384.10/364.60 an ounce against New York's previous close of US$383.90/384.40.
